subject: Dedicated capacity: post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@pulsemed.com>, Ajay Menon <ajay@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sofia / Ajay —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we stay aligned. If I missed anything, please flag and I’ll update.

Key pain points you shared
- High inference cost and noisy latency variability on bursty imaging workloads (peak times see 3-4x baseline).
- Regulatory requirement for tenant isolation and auditability (HIPAA scope for a subset of models).
- Need predictable throughput for scheduled overnight batch processing and low-latency interactive triage during business hours.

Goals we agreed on
- Reserved/dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pool) to guarantee throughput and consistent P95 latency to clinician-facing workflows.
- VPC/private deployment option for the PHI-sensitive models plus RBAC and audit logs.
- SLA targets: uptime >= 99.9% and sustained P95 latency < 250ms for 512-token requests on interactive routes.

Technical recap / sizing notes
- Baseline traffic: ~150k tokens/day today, projected 3x in next 6 months with new imaging pipeline.
- Recommended starting capacity: 4x A100-class GPUs (reserved) with autoscale policy to add 2 GPUs for nightly batch peaks. This provides headroom for forecasted growth and keeps latency under target with batching.
- Isolation: private subnets + customer VPC peering (Redwood Private) for the PHI models; option to run non-PHI models on shared hosted infra to reduce cost.

Deliverables I’ll send by EOD tomorrow (attached)
- Architecture diagram: dedicated cluster + VPC peering and routing notes. [Attachment: architecture_diagram.pdf (application/pdf)]
- Draft SOW with proposed capacity, pricing, and timeline. [Attachment: draft_sow_pulsemed_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
- Pricing sheet with committed monthly costs and burst policy. [Attachment: pricing_sheet_q1_2027.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Next steps / proposed timeline
1) Technical deep-dive with PulseMed infra + Redwood infra engineers (30-60m) — schedule for next week (suggest Wed or Thu).
2) Procurement review of SOW and PO process — Sofia to share procurement contact and timing.
3) Kickoff provisioning once SOW signed: target start of dedicated capacity within 4–6 weeks.

Action items
- Sofia: confirm availability for technical deep-dive and share any additional compliance questions (HIPAA scope, BAAs).
- Ajay: validate the initial capacity recommendation vs. expected nightly batch sizes.
- Ben / Marissa: finalize SOW and pricing, follow up with procurement copy.

Appreciate the time — excited to help PulseMed stabilize latency and control unit economics.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: draft_sow_pulsemed_v1.docx]

From: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@pulsemed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Ajay Menon <ajay@pulsemed.com>, Procurement <procurement@pulsemed.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Ben — this is a great summary and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The HIPAA scope covers PHI-derived clinical notes and structured outputs from the imaging model. We will need BAA language in the SOW and a short write-up of audit log retention (minimum 1 year).
- The batch window peaks are typically between 02:00–05:00 local (roughly 60–80k tokens/hour during peak). Interactive traffic is modest but latency-sensitive (triage UI).
- Procurement: we have a standard PO process and need line-item pricing and a draft contract. I’ve CC’d Procurement (procurement@pulsemed.com).

We’re available for a technical deep-dive Wednesday 2027-02-10 between 10:00–11:00 PT or Thursday 2027-02-11 in the afternoon. Either works for Ajay and me.

Sofia
Sofia Ruiz
Head of Platform Engineering | PulseMed
sofia.ruiz@pulsemed.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: post-call recap & next steps

Looping you both in — Sofia confirmed the BAA requirement and provided the procurement cadence. I made a few notes for the SOW and pricing:

- BAA + audit log retention: add a clause for 12-month audit logs export and monthly access window for compliance audits.
- Capacity: adjust the SOW to start at 4 GPUs reserved with an autoscale policy to +2 for nightly batch. Include a fallback routed to hosted shared instances for non-PHI traffic to help cost.
- SLA: propose 99.9% uptime and P95 latency objective < 250ms for interactive route; include credit calculation and measurement windows.
- Billing: show committed monthly price and an overage rate for burst capacity; include itemized line for private deployment (VPC setup, peering, one-time setup fee).

I’ve attached my redlines and a pricing worksheet. I’ll take the first pass on the SOW and aim to share by EOD today so Ben can send to Sofia/procurement.

Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
